At 25 hours of playtime upon release of the game, you will get at least 25 hours of play time at minimum. If you're a completionist, think more roughly around 75-80 hours if you big brain it and do what you need to do to complete all achievements. The game has a ton to collect, efficency is huge. It will take 300 trips to fully complete the game, don't use the extra time anymore than necessary in a dig. All items will come in time even at 7 min runs. Get as deep as you can and use your bombs. Utilize emergency depots as needed. Collect all the red blocks you can, going to need them for chips to buy cosmetics. There is a ton to learn and improve gameplay as you go. I could write much more.

This game is totally my kind of game. I see that some reviews claim it's too slow or grindy, but I have to disagree. The pacing feels just right. You never get overwhelmed, yet every run gives you meaningful progress. I haven't had a single completed run where I couldn't buy a new upgrade or unlock something new. So I'm honestly not sure what these reviewers mean by "slow progress." As for the other aspects of the game, like the music and the overall atmosphere, they really hit the sweet spot for me. So yeah, I'll definitely keep playing this, and I recommend that anyone who loves digging games does the same!

It's missing something. Not sure what, probably a story and some non-mining stuff like constructing a town or something would be nice. The game was pretty fun for a few hours but there just isn't enough variety in the gameplay loop. You mine blocks, find slot machines, find random chest....and that's it. Also, there is an imbalance with money. It was ok for some time but the value of items as you go deeper falls way behind in the cost of upgrades, forcing you to mine the same zone more and more as you unlock the next zone. Contracts cost a ton of money and the rewards are less than missions for the most part. You also are limited by the number of contracts you can take at once, while you are always working towards all missions. Most of my upgrades for equipment or the mineshaft are $12000+ each. There's 4 different pieces of equipment to upgrade per zone and each zone has 2 mine upgrades. That's $72000 for a single zone. Yet I get about $10000 per run if you count completing missions/contracts. That's 8 runs for the zone I'm in and it is getting exponentially worse at this point. Run value goes up by maybe $500 per zone while each upgrade increases by thousands. For now I can't recommend the game until some more content is added and this money issue is fixed. And if you are a completionist I'm around 60% complete with the collections at this point. So prepare to spend probably 25+ hours.

A really great incremental mining game. I like how the pickaxe can be aimed diagonally, as it allows you to create tunnels sloping up instead of just down. The progress is really satisfying, as there are equipment upgrades, tunnels and ladders, skills, and artifacts that can be collected. Two tweaks that I would suggest: the progress is really good for the first 90% of the game, but the second last and last equipment upgrade tiers slow things down considerably, due to the gold cost. I hit a bottleneck to get the 2nd last pickaxe where I had more than enough materials for it, but had to complete ~4 runs to earn enough gold to afford it, which was a change from the rest of the game where I felt I could buy something consistently after each run. The 2nd tweak would be to allow the entire skill tree to be purchased. Having a level cap seems unnecessary- allow all the skills to be bought, and then offer small incremental increases to stamina, loot slots, or dig speed beyond that.
